episodes.161293: A line of severe thunderstorms produced damaging winds across portions of the Missouri Ozarks.
episodes.161446: Showers and thunderstorms repeatedly moved across Northern Alabama and Southern Middle TN. Numerous roads were closed in Lincoln County, with widespread rainfall amounts of 3-6 across much of the area. Portions of NW Madison received 6-8 over a few hours, leading to flash flooding.
episodes.161498: Strong thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front tracking through the western Great Lakes during the evening hours. The strong storms brought gusty winds as they tracked over the bay of Green Bay and Lake Michigan nearshore waters.
episodes.161976: Showers and thunderstorms developed along and ahead of cold front which moved across the state. A few storms over southeastern Arkansas became strong to severe, with a couple reports of wind damage and one report of hail.
episodes.162312: A trough of low pressure extended across the region with sea  breezes triggering numerous showers and storms over a moist and diurnally unstable airmass. Sea breeze mergers focused the higher rain chances across inland areas where locally heavy rainfall occurred.
episodes.162559: Feeder band moisture and low-level convergence from Tropical Storm Peter, which was located well north of the area, resulted in widespread shower and thunderstorm across the Puerto Rico.
episodes.162622: Thunderstorms developed into northeastern Oklahoma and southwestern Missouri during the evening of the 20th, as a cold front moved into the area. These thunderstorms moved through northwestern Arkansas during the early morning hours of the 21st. The strongest storms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.162659: A waterspout was reported offshore of Panama City Beach in association with a shower.
episodes.162661: Very heavy rainfall in a short period of time over Tallahassee resulted in flash flooding.
episodes.162688: Deep tropical moisture associated with the remnants of Tropical Storm Nicholas was lifted northward ahead of a strong cold front.  Precipitable water values ranging from 1.9 to 2.2 inches were carried into the northwestern portion of North Carolina during the evening of the 21st.  Warm rain processes produced efficient rainfall rates of 2- to 4-inches per hour, enhanced by orographic lift up the Blue Ridge.  Portions of northeast Surry County received locally in excess of nine inches or rain, with FLASH ( Flooded Locations And Simulated Hydrographs Project) Crest Unit Streamflows indicated six-hour Average Recurrence Intervals for this area for rainfall was between a 100- and 200-year event in spots.
episodes.162930: Scattered thunderstorms moved across portions of southern Lake Michigan during the early morning of September 21st.
episodes.163055: As a cold front moved through the region, showers and storms developed. Some of the storms produced damaging winds.
episodes.163061: A cold front moving east across the Upper Midwest propelled a cold front through northwest Wisconsin leading to the development of a line of storms during the afternoon. These storms produced sporadic wind damage and heavy rain and training of the storms led to some minor flash flooding in spots as well. While storms were exhibiting circulation in the low levels, no tornadoes were reported.
episodes.163071: A line of storms rolled across western Wisconsin during the late afternoon and evening of September 20th ahead of a cold front. These storms produced an EF1 tornado that moved across rural areas of northern Trempealeau County. The tornado flipped a semi as it crossed State Highway 93 injuring the driver and then went on to destroy several farm outbuildings and damaged two homes south of Strum (Trempealeau County). The storms also blew down trees near Mindoro (La Crosse County), White Creek (Adams County) and Friendship (Adams County) and removed the roof off a shed west of Bloom City (Richland County).
episodes.163114: A plume of tropical moisture led to multiple rounds of showers and thunderstorms which resulted in flooding and flash flooding.
episodes.163174: Numerous thunderstorms along a cold front moved across southern WI during the evening. A small number of these storms produced damaging winds.
episodes.163243: Clusters of thunderstorms developed along the southeast South Carolina coast in the afternoon and evening hours, producing damaging wind gusts across Beaufort County.
episodes.163252: A line of thunderstorms moved through the area on the evening of September 20. Most of the damage was pretty minor, and outside of one golf ball sized hailstone, all reported hail was around quarter-sized.
episodes.163324: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed in the morning hours and continued into the evening hours on September 20th. There were multiple reports of flash flooding across the area.
episodes.163338: A strong line of thunderstorms pushed through the area along a cold front, with a few embedded thunderstorms that became severe. The main areas that saw some severe weather were along the Highway 34 corridor, where there were several reports of trees down, along with powerlines, due to the strong winds.
episodes.163524: A cluster of storms moved across Lake Michigan early in the morning, resulting in strong wind gusts in excess of 40 mph along the nearshore waters.
episodes.163574: Amidst a prolonged wet and soggy period, another round of heavy rainfall over central Georgia triggered isolated flash flooding through the day on September 20th. Though much of the flooding occurred during the first half of the day, another localized report of flash flooding was reported late in the evening with another round of shower activity.

An automated weather station (Weather Underground: KNCMOUNT12) observed a 24-hour rainfall total, ending 8 AM EDT, of 7.83 inches, which is between a 50- and 100-year rainfall event per NOAA Atlas 14 point frequency estimates for this duration.  This event includes about five inches of rain which fell between 9 PM and midnight on the 21st, which is between a 200- and 500-year event per NOAA Atlas 14.

An automated weather station (Weather Underground: KNCARARA1) observed a 24-hour rainfall total, ending 8 AM EDT, of 6.18 inches, which is about a 25-year rainfall event per NOAA Atlas 14 point frequency estimates for this duration. National Weather Service storm survey revealed straight-line microburst winds caused damage near West 13th Avenue, just west of Pine Bluff. Damage consisted of large tree branches broken, small trees uprooted, concrete-supported posts pulled out of the ground, snapped tree trunks, and a large metal roof canopy being ripped off a barn structure. This roof structure then blew into a home, damaging the home and a garage.

A mesonet station in San Marco measured 2.81 inches of rainfall between 2:30 pm and 4:10 pm. Other rain gauges in the area measured 1.8 to 2.65 inches of rain in about the same time frame.

At 3:57 pm, the public reported street flooding near San Marco Blvd and Lasalle Street. Water was up to the curb and spilling over onto sidewalks. At 4 pm, local broadcast media reported street flooding along San Marco Blvd. Water was nearly up to the top of car tires along the street. At 4:10 pm, the public shared a picture via social media of flood water overflowing Craig Creek. Water was also about 8 inches deep in the backyard of a residence in the area. At 4:20 pm, broadcast media reported street flooding along Lasalle Street and Belmonte Ave and the public reported street flooding at Lasalle St and Hendricks Ave. Multiple vehicles were stuck in flood water in San Marco. At 5:10 pm, the public reported street flooding along Landon Avenue. Doppler radar estimated about 1.8 to 2 inches of rainfall accumulation in 1 hour prior to the onset of flood reports.
